operations.body:
Stage 1 (core) merged 2026-09-12 as PR #133 — https://github.com/dgoings/workbook/pull/133

core.Priority is now a project-configured vocabulary in the shared configuration ledger: definitions, labels, rank order, a default tag, an optional color, rename and retirement forwarding, growth ceilings, arity repair, four conflict types, and the reconcile classifiers. Nothing user-visible changed for a project holding valid history — verified by running base and HEAD binaries against one project created by the base binary.

Raises the writer-format generation to 3. Whatever release gathers this must be release:minor, per the rule the PR adds to CONTRIBUTING.md.

TWO THINGS STAGE 2 MUST HANDLE, both recorded in the PR body and in code:
1. The first priority.add on an unconfigured project would strand every existing task. Reads treat a nil section as the built-in three; the fold starts from nil as empty. One add yields a vocabulary of one while every task is still high/medium/low. A comment beside configPriorities explains why the obvious fixes are not obviously right. Stage 2 must solve this before it ships an authoring path.
2. PriorityVocabulary has no Forwarding() sibling, which is why the priority filter refuses an undefined token where the status filter reports a miss. Stage 2 wants that reporting path.

Starting stage 2 (CLI verbs) on branch feat/priority-cli.
